[system]: Thread: "Spreadsheet app crashes when filtering large table"
[User_Lena]: Hi all, my desktop spreadsheet app (CalcPro 2022 on Windows 10) keeps crashing whenever I try to apply a filter to a table with ~10,000 rows. It just freezes for a few seconds and then closes with no error message. Any idea what I should check?
[SuperUser_Max]: This is a known CalcPro quirk with large datasets. @Lena, first thing: try copying a few hundred rows into a new file and see if filtering still crashes. If it doesn’t, you’re likely hitting a size/performance issue in that original file.
[SuperUser_Max]: Also go into Options > Advanced and turn OFF "Enable hardware acceleration"—we’ve seen that trigger crash-on-filter on some graphics drivers. Restart CalcPro after changing it.
[SuperUser_Kim]: And if you’re still using the older .cpx format, do File > Save As and switch to the .cpw format, then try the filter again. That’s usually the combination that fixes it.

[system]: Thread: "Turning off popup notifications in TeamChat desktop app"
[User_Dan]: I’m trying to stop those little pop-up notifications in the bottom-right corner from TeamChat on Windows 11. I turned off "Show message previews" in the app, but the pop-ups still appear every time someone posts in a busy channel. Is there another setting I’m missing?
[SuperUser_Kim]: Yes. The in-app toggle only changes the content of the notification, not whether Windows shows it. Go to Settings > System > Notifications and scroll down to find TeamChat, then disable notifications for it entirely.
[SuperUser_Max]: If you don’t want to turn them off completely, you can also use Windows "Focus assist" to only show high-priority notifications and exclude TeamChat from that list. That way you won’t see the pop-ups during busy periods.
rounds.response: @Lena — quick checklist to try: 1) Copy a few hundred rows into a new file and see if filtering still crashes. 2) In CalcPro Options > Advanced, turn OFF "Enable hardware acceleration" and restart the app. 3) File > Save As and choose the .cpw format, then test the filter. 4) If it still crashes, open Windows Event Viewer (Windows Logs > Application) right after a crash and note the CalcPro error/faulting module and timestamp. 5) Finally, update CalcPro and your graphics drivers (or try running CalcPro in safe/clean profile) and report any Event Viewer error details here.

rounds.response: Good — back up the file first. Try removing the conditional formats for that column via Format > Conditional Formatting (Manage Rules) and delete any rules scoped to that column, then test the filter. If the rules dialog crashes, work around it by inserting a new blank column, copy the problematic column, Paste Special → Values into the new column (this strips conditional formatting/styles), delete the old column and rename the new one, then reapply clean conditional formats if needed. You can also select the column and use Clear → Clear Formats (or Format > Clear Direct Formatting) to remove cell styles before testing. If it still crashes after those steps, collect the Event Viewer fault entry and calcprographics.dll version and share them or send them to CalcPro support.
